title: Scaling a CUDA-Q GQE + QSCI pipeline to 40 qubits for EUV photoresist chemistry
abstract: We scale a CUDA-Q-native pipeline coupling a generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) to quantum-selected configuration interaction (QSCI) across active spaces of 14 to 44 qubits, applied to the extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) photoresist chemistry of monoalkyltin oxo-hydroxides. A GPT-2 policy emits UCCSD operator sequences; sampled bitstrings become determinants, diagonalised classically, and a cross-circuit generalised-eigenvalue refinement makes every reported GQE+QSCI energy a variational upper bound. Every rung from 14 to 40 qubits carries an exact CASCI or FCI reference, up to 166 million determinants for SnO at 32 qubits. The pipeline is chemically accurate, below 1.6 mHa, through 30 qubits on methyltin trihydroxide and through 32 on SnO, on the best seed at the top rungs. Circuit depth rather than training length is the scaling lever; the refined subspace grows near-linearly with the operator count while staying a vanishing fraction of the determinant space, 0.017% at the 32-qubit SnO rung. It also runs on the 54-qubit IQM Emerald processor, at the shallow depths its routed two-qubit gates allow, reaching +0.330 mHa for SnO at 14 qubits from a CCSD-amplitude-ordered pool prefix and +3.92 mHa for the industrial n-butyltin ligand at 22 qubits from depth-truncated trained circuits under per-circuit readout self-calibration, 81% of the active-space correlation; classical configuration recovery on those counts tightens the 22-qubit result to +0.18 to 0.21 mHa. For the methyl resist, ionisation collapses the classical UCCSD(T) Sn-C bond dissociation energy from 72.6 to 21.2 kcal/mol, the switch that flips solubility on exposure. Against that, the 40-qubit result is support-limited at 22.8 mHa, the full trained ansatz on hardware awaits better fidelities, and classical subspace expansion reaches the 32 to 40-qubit spaces with no quantum sampler, so that boundary is mapped, not beaten.
summary: The authors present a scalable quantum pipeline combining GQE and QSCI to simulate complex bond chemistry in EUV photoresists up to 40 qubits. By leveraging circuit depth as the scaling mechanism, they achieve chemical accuracy benchmarks against exact methods. This work is significant for demonstrating near-term quantum computation's potential in materials informatics.
main_problem: The study addresses simulating bond-breaking chemistry in EUV photoresist materials, which requires methods beyond single-determinant approximations due to multireference character.
main_result: The developed quantum pipeline successfully scales calculations up to 40 qubits while maintaining chemical accuracy for key molecular fragments relevant to lithography. The method demonstrates that circuit depth, rather than training length, is the primary scaling lever.
method: A hybrid computational approach coupling a Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) with Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI), implemented on CUDA-Q and tested on real quantum hardware.
model_or_system: The system models EUV photoresist chemistry, specifically methyltin trihydroxide and n-butyltin trihydroxide, using active spaces ranging from 14 to 44 qubits. Reference calculations are benchmarked against exact CASCI or FCI results for smaller fragments like SnO.
key_observables: Energy error (in mHa), bond dissociation energy changes upon ionization, and the size of the refined quantum subspace relative to the total determinant space.
important_parameters: Qubit count (scaling from 14 to 40 qubits), circuit depth ($L$), and chemical accuracy targets ($\le 1.6 	ext{ mHa}$).
main_assumptions: The full trained ansatz on hardware awaits better fidelities, and the boundary beyond $\sim 32$ qubits is currently mapped by classical subspace expansion rather than quantum mechanical breakthrough.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Active Space Projection (AVAS) regions for both resists, while tables detail error metrics across various qubit rungs comparing GQE+QSCI against other methods.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the chemical problem, detailing the hybrid quantum-classical pipeline (GQE $ightarrow$ QSCI), demonstrating successful scaling and accuracy benchmarks on smaller systems ($	ext{SnO}$), and finally applying this to complex resist chemistry up to 40 qubits.
why_interesting: This work pushes the boundaries of simulating strongly correlated electronic structure problems relevant to materials science, using quantum machine learning techniques (GPT-2 policy) to manage exponentially large Hilbert spaces on near-term hardware.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The hybrid system. GPT-2 policy (GPU) → CUDA-Q circuit sampling (single-GPU fp32 statevector to 32q; pooled 4-GPU mgpu at 34q via a persistent containerised worker; tensornet-mps at 40q; real IQM Emerald via the native iqm target) → classical QSCI diagonalisation and GEVP refinement → loss update, with classical post-processing of the sampled subspace (details in Table 1).

Figure 2: The AVAS active-space regions, tinted as in Table 1. Left and centre, the resist CH3Sn(OH)3: the Sn-C space, the EUV solubility switch (AVAS Sn 5s, Sn 5p, C 2p; 22q and 26q), then the added Sn-O crosslinking network (+O 2p; 30q and up). Right, the industrial ligand n-BuSn(OH)3: its AVAS label is atom-indexed on the alpha carbon, so the rest of the chain stays outside the active space and the ligand occupies the same (14e,11o) space at 22q as the methyl resist, the one rung at which it is run.

Figure 3: Circuit depth closes the scaling gap (best seed, fixed 200-iteration budget and determinant cap; GEVP-refined error against each system’s exact CASCI). (a) Error falls with the generated-operator count 𝐿: the SnO 24, 28 and 32q rungs enter the chemical-accuracy band (shaded) from 3.36, 8.64 and 10.06 mHa at 𝐿 = 10. (b) Mechanism: the cross-circuit GEVP subspace grows near-linearly with 𝐿; the resist’s concentrated 24-electron wavefunction grows an order of magnitude more slowly, the origin of its saturation (broken at 𝐿 = 600, see text).

Figure 4: The EUV switch in CH3Sn(OH)3 at 22 qubits. (a) The radical cation’s Sn-C dissociation surface: GEVP-refined QSCI energies ride the exact doublet CASCI curve out to 4.25 Å, two thirds of the way to the asymptote; the neutral curve (grey) is far steeper, and the dashed orange line is the CH3 radical plus charged Sn(OH)3 frozen-fragment gap at UCCSD(T). Ionisation collapses the classical UCCSD(T) bond-dissociation energy from 72.6 to 21.2 kcal/mol. (b) Per-point error against the chemical-accuracy band, with the active-space CCSD(T) deviation, the best of four seeds where run, and the Mulliken spin on CH3 (right axis) tracking the channel.
